title: Permissions and users
intro: Every file has an owner, a group and read/write/execute bits for each. You're root here, so you can create users and see the rules from both sides.

steps.text: Who am I, and which groups am I in?
Make a script and look at its permission bits.
steps.cmd: printf '#!/bin/sh\necho it runs\n' > hello.sh && ls -l hello.sh

steps.text: Try to run it. It fails: there's no x bit.
Add execute permission for the owner, then run it.
Numeric modes: 640 is rw- for owner, r-- for group, nothing for others.
Become that user. Notice the prompt changes from # to $.
As student, you can't read root's home.
